description: American Labor looks at work from the worker’s side: workplace concerns, the history and role of unions, how bargaining works, and how owners, employees and communities balance their goals.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words. Excerpts confirmed requirements 1, 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8; requirements 2 and 6 were not visible in current form and are not outlined yet.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)

requirements.title: Concerns of workers
requirements.summary: Learning about working people and listing major concerns of American workers, including researching a labor organization.

requirements.title: What unions do
requirements.summary: What labor unions are, what they do and what services they provide.

requirements.title: Bargaining
requirements.summary: Union terms and the difference between adversarial and cooperative bargaining.

requirements.title: Labor history project
requirements.summary: One option, such as a timeline, an exhibit, a film discussion or a biography.

requirements.title: Both sides of an issue
requirements.summary: Arguing a current labor issue from management’s side and then from labor’s.

requirements.title: Goals and compromise
requirements.summary: The different goals of owners, shareholders, customers, employees, unions, communities and officials, and why they compromise.
